transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic? What's been concerning you?

Hi. Well, I came in today because... I've been feeling a lot more tense and down than I expected lately. I recently tried to clean up my image and my routine for some arts board stuff I'm involved with, and it's just been getting to me. 

I mean, I'm still doing the basics of my day, but I just keep dropping little things that I normally really care about—like my fair planning notes or my design drafts. And then I just feel guilty about falling behind, and I end up canceling plans with people instead of actually catching up on what I missed. It's just been frustrating.
When you think about what's been bothering you most over the past few weeks, would you say it's more the feeling of sadness and low mood, or more the feeling of worry and tension?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. It's hard to separate them. I guess... I get worried and tense about falling behind on my stuff, and then that just makes me feel down and sad that I'm messing it up. So I don't really know if one is bothering me more than the other. They just kind of go together.
You mentioned trying to clean up your image and routine for the arts board—how long ago did that start, and would you say these feelings of tension and sadness began around the same time?

Well, the whole image reset started a little while ago. I basically started changing my clothes, my daily routines, and even who I was spending time with, just to fit the arts board better. 

And, yeah, I started feeling this way a few weeks after I began doing all of that. It wasn't right away, but maybe a few weeks into trying to keep up with all those changes is when the tension and sadness really started to hit me.
When you think back to those first few weeks after you started making all those changes for the arts board, did the worried and tense feelings start before the sadness, or did the sadness come first?

I'm honestly not really sure which one came first. It's kind of a blur looking back. I just remember feeling overwhelmed by the whole thing, but I couldn't tell you if I felt anxious before I felt sad, or the other way around. They just sort of crept up on me together, I guess.
When you're not thinking about the arts board or your work falling behind, do you still feel that tension and worry, or does it mainly come up when you're dealing with those specific things?

I think... it's mostly when I'm dealing with those specific things. Like, if I'm just watching a movie or talking to a friend about something totally unrelated, I don't feel as tense. It really just hits me when I think about the board, or when I realize I'm falling behind on my own work because I'm spending so much energy trying to fit in.
Over the past few weeks, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy levels—like sleeping more or less than usual, eating differently, or feeling physically exhausted?

I haven't really noticed any big changes with those things. My sleep seems pretty much the same as always, and I'm eating about the same amount. I guess I feel a little tired sometimes, but not like, physically exhausted or anything out of the ordinary.
Even on days when you're not thinking about the arts board or your work, do you find yourself worrying about other things—like your health, finances, relationships, or just things in general?

No, not really. I mean, if I'm not thinking about the board or my work, I'm usually fine. I don't really sit around worrying about my health or money or anything like that. It's pretty much just tied to the board stuff.

When you do think about the arts board or your work falling behind, how much of your day would you say you're spending worried or tense about it—is it just a few minutes here and there, or is it taking up a significant chunk of your time throughout the day?

I'd say it takes up a significant chunk of time, yeah. It's not just a few minutes... it's more like, if I'm trying to work on my own stuff, the worry about the board just kind of sits there in the back of my mind. And then I start thinking about how I'm falling behind, and I get tense. So it definitely stretches out over the day when I'm trying to get things done.

If you think about situations outside of the arts board—like social situations, work deadlines, or other responsibilities you care about—do you find yourself getting worried or tense about those things too, or is it really just the board that triggers this for you?

No, it's really just the board. I mean, I have other things going on, but they don't make me feel tense like this. If I have a regular deadline or I'm hanging out with people, I feel totally fine. It's just... the board stuff is what gets to me.

You mentioned the tension and worry are really tied to the arts board. But I want to make sure I'm understanding this correctly—when you're NOT actively thinking about or working on the board, do you still feel that underlying sense of worry or tension in your body, or does it pretty much go away completely?

It pretty much goes away completely. If I'm doing something else and my mind is totally off of it, I feel fine. I don't really carry that physical tension around unless the board stuff pops back into my head.
When you imagine having to quit the arts board or step back from it completely, how would you feel? Would the worry and tension go away, or do you think you'd still feel anxious about other things?

If I stepped back completely? I think... yeah, the worry and tension would definitely just go away. I really don't think I'd be anxious about other things. 

Because, I mean, the whole reset with the board is still going on right now. It's not like this is some separate anxiety problem I'm having that's continuing long after the changes ended. The changes are still happening. So if I just wasn't part of it anymore, I'm pretty sure I'd feel totally fine again.
